name: National Bank Holdings Corporation

sections.title: Diluted earnings per share by quarter
sections.callout: Q4 2025: diluted EPS of $0.42, down from $0.73 a year earlier.

footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. From pre-tax income to net income to common: after income tax and $880K of preferred dividends & other. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Diluted EPS by quarter as reported in the 10-Qs; fourth quarters are calculated (net income ÷ estimated diluted shares) because EPS does not add across quarters.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 2.3% to $416M in 2025. Net interest income rose 0.9% to $349M and noninterest income rose 10.3% to $67.6M; noninterest expense rose 3.9%, and the provision for credit losses was $17.8M, versus $6.8M.
Net income to common fell 8.5% to $109M, or $2.85 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 63.6% versus 62.6%. National Bank Holdings returned $61.2M through dividends and buybacks.

risks: Changes in general business and economic conditions as well as external events such as natural disasters, pandemics, cyberattacks…
Our business is highly susceptible to credit risk and fluctuations in the value of real estate and other collateral securing such credit
Like other financial services institutions, our asset and liability structures are monetary in nature
The value of our mortgage and SBA servicing rights can decline during periods of falling interest rates…
We may not be able to meet the cash flow requirements of deposit withdrawals and other business needs unless we maintain sufficient liquidity
strategy: Focus on client-centered, relationship-driven banking strategy
Expansion of commercial banking, business banking and specialty businesses
Expansion through organic growth, competitive product and digital offerings
Continue to strengthen profitability through organic growth and operating efficiencies
Maintain conservative risk profile and sound risk management practices
